parole.significato: A form of Okinawan folk dance.
bitter melon (edible fruit, especially as it is eaten by Okinawans)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Okinawan ごーやー (gooyaa).

parole.significato: A weapon originating from Okinawa, Japan, consisting of two sticks joined by a chain or cord.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Okinawan 双節棍 (nunchaku) (compare Japanese 双節棍 (nunchaku)), probably from Hokkien 兩節棍 /两节棍 (nn̄g-chat-kùn, literally “two-segment cudgel”), from 兩 /两 (nn̄g, “two”) + 節 /节 (chat, “joint; link; segment”) + 棍 (kùn, “cudgel; stick”).
Borrowed from Okinawan 酒 (さき, saki). Doublet of sake.

parole.significato: A citrus fruit, native to Taiwan and Okinawa (Citrus reticulata, syn. Citrus depressa)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Okinawan シークワーサー.
